tasks.short: Assign clients to support workers, supervise them in case discussions, follow their notes, check their reports and send approved reports to referrers.

steps.what: Mental health social worker assigns clients to support workers in the weekly team meeting
Mental health social worker supervises and directs support workers in case discussions
Mental health social worker reads support workers' notes to follow up clients
Mental health social worker checks support workers' reports for referrers: content against the notes, the referrer's question and what may be shared
Mental health social worker sends each checked report to the referrer through secure messaging from the record

tasks.design: A caseload view in the client record ({OTHER}) shows per support worker which clients have missed appointments, overdue plans or new notes, so the social worker reads what needs attention instead of every file. Reports approved by the social worker go to referrers through secure messaging from the record. Assigning, supervising and checking stay with the social worker; the view is not used to rate support workers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Files were opened one by one to follow up, and reports sent by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Client records offer caseload views and secure messaging to referrers.
tasks.still_hard: What a support worker leaves out of a note does not show in any view.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing in supervision that a worker is close to burnout.

reach.learn: Whether flagged follow-ups reach supervision sooner.

evidence.claim: Client records can show caseload views with missed appointments and overdue plans.
The GGZ dossier is kept 20 years.

assumptions: Boundary: from new referrals to reports sent; hiring support workers is outside.
Input contract: notes by support workers in the client record; referrals from GPs and the municipality; fallback is opening each file.
Assigning, supervising and checking reports do not change. s5 keeps 20 for sending each report from the record.
Support workers' time is outside the social worker's savings.
research_questions: Are overdue plans picked up sooner?

already_counted.description: Mental health social worker reviews the caseload view.

incremental.description: Mental health social worker keeps flag rules current.

approvals.approved_version: Each report exactly as checked by the social worker in s4, sent once through secure messaging to the referrer named in the record; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the flags miss much, so the social worker still opens most files and s3 keeps 85 (7.2); high: the caseload view as designed (13.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read recent notes and scores for changes in the client's status, discuss them with the client, consult the psychiatrist or team, rewrite the treatment plan, and have the client agree to it.

steps.what: Mental health social worker reads recent notes and scores to see changes in client status
Mental health social worker discusses the changes with the client
Mental health social worker consults the psychiatrist or team about the change
Mental health social worker modifies the treatment plan according to the changes in client status
Mental health social worker checks the final plan: changed goals and actions against the client's view and the team's advice
Mental health social worker offers the checked plan to the client in the portal or on paper for agreement
Client reads and signs the updated plan on paper

tasks.design: A client timeline in the record ({OTHER}) shows recent notes, questionnaire scores and missed appointments together, so changes in status are seen without paging through notes. The treatment plan module keeps the current goals as fields; the social worker edits what changes and the client agrees in the portal or on paper. Discussing with the client and consulting the team stay with the social worker; no model writes the plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes were found by reading back through notes, and plans rewritten as documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Client records offer timelines with scores and plan modules with goal fields.
tasks.still_hard: Status changes often show in what a client does not say.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a missed appointment signals relapse, not forgetfulness.

reach.learn: Whether the timeline shortens team consultations.

evidence.claim: Client records offer timelines of notes and scores and plan modules with goal fields.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the client record to the agreed plan; treatment itself is outside.
Input contract: notes and scores by the treatment team in the record; fallback is reading notes.
Clients agree in the portal or on paper; about the same time, priced as customer time.
Discussing, consulting and checking the plan do not change. s4 keeps 75 because the social worker still writes every change; only retyping unchanged goals goes.
research_questions: Are plans updated sooner after a change?

already_counted.description: Mental health social worker reviews the client timeline.

incremental.description: Mental health social worker helps clients who cannot use the portal.

approvals.approved_version: The updated treatment plan exactly as checked by the social worker in s4b, offered once to that client for agreement in the portal or on paper; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many changes come from conversations not in the record, so s1 keeps 85 (10.0); high: notes and scores kept current by the team (15.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain illness, medication or abuse to clients and families, look up community resources, assemble an information packet, send it, and give talks to community groups.

steps.what: Mental health social worker educates clients about mental illness, abuse and medication
Mental health social worker looks up available community resources for the client
Mental health social worker assembles an information packet for the client
Mental health social worker checks the final packet: each entry fits the client's need, leaflets are current, and the client's address
Mental health social worker sends the checked packet to the client through secure mail
Mental health social worker gives talks to community groups about mental illness

tasks.design: A maintained social map of local services ({DOCS}) is searched by need and area, and each result quotes the service's own entry, so no advice is generated. The packet is assembled from the chosen entries and vetted leaflets by template, and once the social worker has checked it, it goes to the client through secure mail. Educating clients and community talks stay with the social worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resources were found from memory and loose lists, and packets put together by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Municipal social maps list services by need and area.
tasks.still_hard: Social maps go out of date as services change.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which service will actually call a client back.
tasks.altitude: The social worker picks from a current map instead of searching.

evidence.claim: Municipal social maps list local services by need and area.
Health data are special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from client needs to the packet sent and talks given; referrals themselves are outside.
Input contract: social map kept by the municipality's neighbourhood team; vetted leaflets from the organisation; fallback is personal lists.
Educating, talks and checking the packet do not change. s4 keeps 20 for sending it.
Clients read the packet as they read paper leaflets today.
research_questions: Do clients reach the services they were pointed to?

incremental.description: Mental health social worker reports outdated entries in the social map.

approvals.approved_version: The information packet with the chosen service entries and leaflets exactly as checked by the social worker in s3b, sent once through secure mail to that client; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the social map is out of date, so personal lists stay in use and s2 keeps 80 and s3 keeps 70 (10.7); high: a current map (23.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet family members to explain the client's condition, counsel them on coping and support, refer them to support groups, and note family contacts in the record.

steps.what: Mental health social worker meets family members to explain the client's condition
Mental health social worker counsels family members in dealing with and supporting the client
Mental health social worker refers family members to support groups
Mental health social worker writes a note of the family contact in the record

loop.input: The social worker's spoken note dictated after the meeting; the family conversation itself is not recorded.
loop.output: A structured contact note in the record's template.
loop.check: A validator flags any risk statement (suicide, violence, abuse) that is not in the dictation. The social worker reads every note against the dictation and the meeting, checks it says what was said and nothing more, and approves it; unclear notes are typed.
loop.stop: No unapproved note is saved; after one failed redraft the social worker types it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Spoken notes need structuring into the template; plain transcription leaves that to the worker.

tasks.design: Support groups for families are found in the same social map used for clients. After the meeting, the social worker dictates a short note that a speech step turns into the record's template; a validator flags any risk statement not in the dictation, and the social worker approves every note. Meeting and counselling families stay with the social worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after meetings, often at the end of the day.
tasks.enabler_now: Dictation tools turn spoken notes into structured reports in care records.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted notes have been found to contain statements nobody made.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a parent accept a child's diagnosis without blame.

evidence.claim: Attendi's dictation turns spoken notes into a SOEP report in GGZ and other care settings.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation in AI-written notes.

assumptions: Boundary: from the family's request to the contact note; the client's treatment is outside.
Input contract: social map from the municipality; dictation by the social worker; fallback is typing.
Meeting and counselling do not change. s4 keeps 75 because the social worker still composes and reads every note; the speech step only removes typing and layout.
Family members' time does not change.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a risk statement?

already_counted.description: Mental health social worker reads and approves each drafted note.

incremental.description: Mental health social worker reports wrong drafts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the social map lists few family groups and dictation is often weak, so s3 keeps 85 and s4 keeps 90 (2.5); high: map and dictation as designed (7.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The mental health social worker keeps supervising, treatment decisions, educating and counselling families; paging through files, searching resources and typing notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Checking drafted notes for invented statements
role.ambitious_version: A social worker who spends saved time with clients and families.

job.title: Mental Health and Substance Abuse Social Workers
